provenance_as_recorded.snapshot_scope: All 72 tracked Python files from original commit, sufficient for identical solve_problem API; unrelated historical benchmark data/docs excluded.

timing_semantics: result.seconds is the unchanged solve_problem elapsed time, including session and worker startup/shutdown. Imports, input parsing, report serialization and saving are excluded. The only adapter observer inside that time snapshots spawned worker PIDs at pool shutdown; its small overhead is common to both versions and not quantified. No profiling contexts, worker wrappers or query observers are installed.

skipped_cases.reason: User explicitly requested skipping the slow final case; partial original run and not-started current run excluded.

equivalence.equivalence_scope: Chosen queries, answers, candidates, winner, termination, expected values and recorded candidate volumes/shares; excludes elapsed timers and cache statistics. No complete nonchosen recursive tree or branch-probability comparison.

limitations: Eight measured pairs on one machine, one run per version/case; elapsed gains are observations, not statistical or universal guarantees.
D7 problem 3 was explicitly skipped at the user request; the partial original run and unstarted current run are excluded.
576 compared float pairs cover the stated saved-result scope, not the complete unchosen recursive tree or all branch probabilities.
Spawned worker PIDs are a pool-lifecycle observation; there is no worker-task instrumentation in this comparison.
Raw evidence paths refer to the original external output bundle; archives, logs and profiler data are intentionally not embedded.
snapshot_layout: Exact-bit-equal non-timing semantic results are stored once per paired case. Each version retains its own elapsed total, per-query timings, selection, termination and worker PIDs.
